authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)

description.en: Food license or registration issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) to food business operators, mandatory for all entities involved in manufacturing, processing, packaging, storage, distribution, or sale of food products in India.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Petty food manufacturers, small retailers, hawkers, itinerant vendors, and temporary stall holders with annual turnover up to Rs. 12 lakhs
verifiedConditions.claim: Basic FSSAI Registration is required for petty food business operators with annual turnover not exceeding Rs. 12 lakhs. This includes small retailers, hawkers, itinerant vendors, temporary stall holders, and small-scale food manufacturers.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Medium-sized food businesses with annual turnover between Rs. 12 lakhs and Rs. 20 crore
verifiedConditions.claim: State FSSAI License is required for food businesses with annual turnover exceeding Rs. 12 lakhs but not exceeding Rs. 20 crore. This includes medium-sized manufacturers, storage units, transporters, retailers, marketers, and distributors.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: Large food businesses with annual turnover exceeding Rs. 20 crore
verifiedConditions.claim: Central FSSAI License is required for food businesses with annual turnover exceeding Rs. 20 crore, businesses operating in two or more states, importers, operators in airports/seaports, and government establishments with food catering for over 100 persons.

verifiedConditions.appliesTo: All food business operators in India
verifiedConditions.claim: Every food business operator in India must obtain either a Registration or License from FSSAI before commencing food business operations as per the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

unverifiedEligibility: Central License is also required for businesses operating in central government agencies, railways, and food businesses with imported food items irrespective of turnover.
Specific product categories (dairy, meat processing, proprietary food) may have additional eligibility considerations.
This record does not cover the conversion from registration to license or upgrades between license types.

requirements.claim: Application form (Form A for Basic Registration, Form B for State/Central License) must be filled with details of the food business operator, type of business, food categories, and production capacity.
Photo identity proof of the food business operator (Aadhaar, PAN, Voter ID, or Passport) is required.
Proof of address of the food business premises (ownership deed, rent agreement, utility bill, or NOC from the premises owner) is required.

A food safety management system plan or self-inspection checklist is required. For State and Central licenses, a detailed food safety management plan based on the nature of the business (HACCP plan for large manufacturers) is required.
NOC from the local municipal corporation or panchayat is required for the business premises.
Photographs of the food business premises showing the layout, equipment, storage areas, and processing areas are required.
Water test report from a recognized laboratory may be required for manufacturing and processing units.
A complete list of food products to be manufactured, processed, stored, or sold must be provided with the application.
Partnership deed, Certificate of Incorporation, MOA/AOA, or other constitutional document is required for businesses that are not sole proprietorships.

processInformation.claim: Determine the appropriate license type based on annual turnover and nature of business: Basic Registration (up to Rs. 12 lakhs), State License (Rs. 12 lakhs to Rs. 20 crore), or Central License (above Rs. 20 crore or operating across states).
Register on the FoSCoS (Food Safety Compliance System) portal at foscos.fssai.gov.in. Create an account and log in to access the application forms.

Fill the online application form (Form A for Basic Registration, Form B for State/Central License) with all required details including FBO details, business type, food categories, production capacity, and premises information.
Upload all required documents including identity proof, address proof, food safety management plan, NOC, premises photographs, product list, and any applicable additional documents.

Pay the applicable fee online. Basic Registration fee is Rs. 100 per year. State License fee ranges from Rs. 2000 to Rs. 5000 per year depending on business type. Central License fee is Rs. 7500 per year.

The application is reviewed by the designated FSSAI officer. For State and Central licenses, an inspection of the premises may be conducted. The officer may approve, reject, or seek additional information.

Upon approval, the FSSAI Registration Certificate or License is issued with a 14-digit FSSAI number. The certificate/license is valid for 1-5 years as chosen by the applicant and must be displayed at the business premises. The FSSAI logo and license number must be displayed on food product packaging.

output.claim: An FSSAI Registration Certificate (for basic registration) or FSSAI License (for state/central license) is issued containing the 14-digit FSSAI registration/license number, name and address of the FBO, kind of business, food categories, validity period, and conditions. The FSSAI number must be displayed on all food product labels and packaging.

fees.applicability: Basic FSSAI Registration (annual turnover up to Rs. 12 lakhs)
fees.claim: Basic FSSAI Registration fee is Rs. 100 per year. For a 5-year registration, the total fee is Rs. 500.

fees.applicability: State FSSAI License (annual turnover Rs. 12 lakhs to Rs. 20 crore)
fees.claim: State FSSAI License fee ranges from Rs. 2000 to Rs. 5000 per year depending on the type and scale of food business activity.

fees.applicability: Central FSSAI License (annual turnover above Rs. 20 crore or multi-state operations)
fees.claim: Central FSSAI License fee is Rs. 7500 per year.

fees.applicability: Applicable for delayed renewal of license/registration
fees.claim: A late fee of Rs. 100 per day of delay may be charged for delayed renewal, subject to a maximum amount.

processingTime.claim: Processing time varies by license type. Basic Registration is typically processed within 7 working days. State License processing takes 30-60 days including inspection. Central License processing takes 30-60 days. If no response is received within 60 days of application, the license is deemed to have been granted.

sources.title: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India — Official Portal
sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The FSSAI portal provides official information on food licensing and registration including types of licenses, eligibility criteria based on turnover, document requirements, fee structure, and processing timelines.
claimsSupported: FSSAI registration/license is mandatory for all food business operators.
Three types: Basic Registration, State License, and Central License based on turnover.
Basic Registration for turnover up to Rs. 12 lakhs, State License up to Rs. 20 crore, Central License above Rs. 20 crore.
Basic Registration fee is Rs. 100/year, Central License fee is Rs. 7500/year.
Applications are processed through the FoSCoS portal.
14-digit FSSAI number is issued and must be displayed on food products.
sources.uncertainty: State License fees vary by business type. Processing times may vary based on the type of food business and completeness of application.

sources.title: FoSCoS — Food Safety Compliance System
sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: FoSCoS is the official online platform for FSSAI license and registration applications, renewals, and compliance management. It provides the application forms, document upload facility, fee payment, and application tracking.
claimsSupported: FoSCoS is the official online platform for FSSAI applications.
Form A is used for Basic Registration and Form B for State/Central License.
Applications are submitted, tracked, and managed entirely online.
Fee payment is done online through the portal.
sources.uncertainty: Portal uptime and functionality may vary. Some states may have additional integration requirements.

sources.title: Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
sources.publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 establishes FSSAI and mandates licensing and registration of food businesses under Section 31. The FSS (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 prescribe the detailed requirements.
claimsSupported: Section 31 mandates that every food business operator shall obtain a license or registration.
Operating without a license or registration is an offence under the Act.
The Act empowers FSSAI to prescribe conditions for granting licenses.
If no decision is made within 60 days, the license is deemed granted.
FSSAI number must be displayed on food labels as per labeling regulations.
sources.uncertainty: The Act has been supplemented by multiple regulations and amendments. Specific product-level standards and requirements may apply additionally.

limitations: This record covers the general FSSAI licensing and registration framework. Product-specific standards and requirements (e.g., dairy, meat, organic food) are not individually modeled.
State License fee amounts vary by business type and are not fully enumerated.
The record does not cover FSSAI license modification, renewal, or cancellation processes in detail.
Import-specific requirements for Central License are mentioned but not fully detailed.
Food safety management system requirements (HACCP, GMP, GHP) are mentioned at a high level only.
The record does not cover food recall procedures or penalty provisions under the Act.

review.reviewReason: Core FSSAI licensing framework is reviewed, but product-specific standards, import requirements, and detailed food safety management system requirements need additional coverage.
